context:
Goal: stop the double CI run you asked to stop four times (Oct 31 14:12 CDT, Nov 1 20:51 CST, Nov 10, and now Nov 14).
Problem (goal): a ready PR that is fully green is refused at merge when main gained records after it went ready, and the remedy is draft, records step, ready again, then a second full CI (first measured wall of that second run: 44 min 32 s, one run, n=1: run 43583006785 (pull_request, #3349 head 3128df369), 09:58:07Z to 10:42:39Z, read by the coordinator by REST at 04:49 CST Nov 14. Runner 10's earlier "about 70 min, n=2" was recalled, not read. Two full runs on #3349's head before the records step took 41 and 51 min: 43579044324 and 43564208386) (PR #3349). Triage's approximate count: the committed records page differs from the first parent in 4 of 11 PR-merge commits since Nov 13 and 20 of 38 since Nov 10 (shallow clone, some merges missed), so a ready PR meets this often. Only you can widen a guard.
Based on (record): decision records-index-at-merge (read by triage; its sentence "That batch still runs CI twice (unmeasured in other repos; none in this repo, Oct 24 to 31)" no longer holds). Based on (read, relayed): the lane of step records-page-before-ready read the files and ran nothing: a rebuild in the merge commit is out (push-skip-on-proven-tree needs main's tree to equal the PR head's tree; the merge tool's API merge cannot change the tree); a main-side refresh PR deadlocks as is (main's own lint/hook_catalog.py --check fails a stale page on a push to main; a red main lets only a revert merge). Unmeasured: the lane did not run main's red-main brake against a failing --check push.
Departs from: main — main refuses a ready PR with a stale page and main's check fails any stale page on a push; option a merges that PR as it is, opens a draft refresh PR after it, and waives main's check for the records-only case; option b changes nothing.
Meanwhile: the lane writes the red test and the decision-record edit only and changes no merge.py or hook_catalog.py until you pick; runner 10 runs the remedy on each stale PR (the second run stays).
No option is starred: the only option that meets your ask widens a guard, and by your ruling a widening is never the recommended option; the coordinator's read is that option a is the only route that stops the double run without a push to main.
Added 04:09 CST (records lane's read via the coordinator, 04:08; the coordinator did not read the files; not read by triage): the consultant's candidate to reuse the green run when a push changes only the records page cannot work as stated, because ci-scope.sh diffs the whole PR against its base (line 17), never the push. A form that would work is option c: ci-scope.sh reads the push's before-head, checks that head's run was fully green and the push changed docs/records.md alone, then sets every job flag false; all-jobs-passed counts those skipped jobs as passed. It changes ci-scope.sh, checks.yml and lint/test_ci_scope.py. It edits the script's own fail-safe list, so it needs review round 3 and the net-value test. Unmeasured: the gain (jobs flagged false still start and skip).
Added 04:23 CST (the records lane's own message, stamped 04:24; not read by triage): the lane recommends keeping the refusal (option b below). Triage does not star it. The lane's letters differ from this page's: its (c) is this page's b, its (b narrowed) is this page's a, its (i') is this page's c. Measured by the lane in a scratch copy of main 4db2a9cf3 (read and run): `lint/hook_catalog.py --check` fails a stale page on a push to main and waives it on a PR run. The refusal sits at merge/merge.py:3344. The lane builds nothing while waiting; its record edit (PR #3396, draft) is done.
Added 05:14 CST (runner 10 via the coordinator, 05:15; not read by triage; cost not timed): on draft #3377 the records step pushed a records-page commit (head 732293c9b3 to 8c4dfb4219ed) and made its review record stale, so #3377 now waits on a fix check. For #3349 it did not (docs-only). So for a guard or check PR, option b (keep the refusal) also costs a new head, a lane lint cycle and a fix check. A data point, not a ruling.
Added 05:28 CST (runner 11 via the coordinator, 05:29; logs not read by the coordinator or triage): degen #718 hit this refusal on a ready PR, the first time in degen. The remedy was followed: draft, `merge 718 --confirm` on the draft pushed the records page (head 0d3422ed to b937d1bed), marked ready 05:28. The green run on 0d3422ed no longer covers the new head, so full CI runs again; the last degen run took 14 min and mutation-report 9 min 48 s (n=1, runner 11). Runner 11 suggests a lane pre-runs `merge <pr> --confirm` on its draft before hand-in; the coordinator notes that does not help when another merge lands first (the page changes in about 1 merge in 3 to 1 in 2, triage's approximate count). No lane was told; it is a process change and this item is open.
Corrected 04:24 CST Nov 14: every "about 70 min" above is withdrawn; the first measure is in Problem (44 min 32 s, n=1). Past measured: a full checks run on #3349's head took 41 and 51 min; the coordinator's own reads, earlier tonight: #3376 ready-to-green 79 min (52 of them queued for macOS) and #3279 about 72 min, one each, not after a records step.

options.gain: The second CI run on each records-changing merge goes away; no push to main.
options.label: Merge a ready green PR whose only difference is a records page gone stale, push nothing, then open a draft refresh PR; main's check waives that case on a push to main only (a widening of a guard)
options.lose: Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo. The merge tool stops refusing one case and main's check gains a waiver; one refresh PR per records change; a wrong waiver would let a stale or hand-edited page through (the lane keeps any other stale page failing); not yet tried against the red-main brake.

options.gain: No guard changes; nothing new to review.
options.label: Keep the refusal: the PR goes back to draft, runs the records step, and gets a second CI
options.lose: A second full CI run (44 min 32 s in the one run measured, n=1) on each ready PR that meets a records-changing merge first (about 1 merge in 3 to 1 in 2 by triage's count); your fourth repeat of the ask stays unmet.

options.gain: A records-page push on a green PR costs minutes of CI, not a second full run; no change to the merge tool or to main's check.
options.label: Let CI scope skip every job on a push that changes only docs/records.md when the head before the push was fully green (a widening of a guard)
options.lose: Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo. The merged tree rests on a green run of the head before the push, read from GitHub, not a run of that tree; it edits the CI scope script's own fail-safe list; the gain is unmeasured.

short: Let a ready green PR merge when only the records page went stale, or keep the refusal and the second CI?
title: A ready, green PR is refused when main gained records after it went ready, and a second full CI follows. May the merge tool merge it as it is and refresh the page in a draft PR after, with main's check waived for that case only (a), keep the refusal and the second CI (b), or skip CI on a records-only push after a green head (c)?
why: You asked four times to stop the double CI run. The routes that avoid widening a guard are out by the lane's reads, so the one that meets your ask removes a refusal and adds a waiver on main's check, which only you grant.
